title: ralph-task-monitor never sees agent output in production: reads input.tool_result.{stdout,content,text} while the harness delivers tool_response — resultText is always empty and all three detection tiers are unreachable
causal_links: with D2d-04, both Ralph hook-side task-state updaters are dead — explains reliance on manual ralph-checkpoint/state edits
observe_how: Same event, same matcher (PostToolUse matcher=Agent, verified registered): sibling hook agent-error-capture reads input.tool_response; ralph-task-monitor reads input.tool_result. Both cannot be right. shared/types.ts declares tool_response as the canonical PostToolUseInput field. With tool_result absent, resultText is '' and the hook returns at line 327 before structured-JSON/XML/pattern detection or any Braintrust agent_task_success emit — so during live Ralph runs, agent completions never auto-update .ralph/state.json from the Task path. Unit tests pass because they feed tool_result directly (test-only contract). Observe by running a Ralph session and checking that no 'RALPH TASK MONITOR:' additionalContext ever appears after Task completions.
telemetry: agent_task_success Braintrust emits from this hook: effectively 0 in production; corr-null 60.7% and 30/36 agents never in agent-recall are consistent with Task-side PostToolUse consumers not seeing payloads

title: agent-error-capture (and hook-error-pipeline) shell out to store_learning.py via execSync string concatenation with only quote/newline escaping — on Windows cmd.exe, error content containing \" or metachars breaks quoting; this is the junk-file creation mechanism family of SEED-01
causal_links: candidate mechanism for SEED-01 junk artifacts
D2d-07 (over-broad triggers raise how often hostile content reaches this shell path)
observe_how: The content fed to --content is raw agent error output (stack traces, code snippets) which routinely contains ", >, &, |, ^ and %. Escaping handles only " and newline; on Windows, execSync runs via cmd.exe where backslash-escaped quotes do not reliably keep cmd's own quote state — a " in content toggles quoting and any following > or & becomes live redirection/chaining, creating stray files in cwd (opcDir = opc/) — matching the SEED-01 artifact location ('junk files under opc/', also recorded at ROADMAP.md:197 finding (a)). The codebase already has the safe pattern in the SAME file family: post-plan-roadmap, smarter-everyday, periodic-extract and browser-learning-extractor all use spawn with an args ARRAY (no shell). Fix: convert agent-error-capture.ts:176 and hook-error-pipeline.ts:103 to spawnSync('uv', [args...]). Note: SEED-01's daily ~07:24 writer still needs the Task-Scheduler probe — these two hooks are event-driven, so they are the mechanism family, not necessarily the scheduled invoker.
telemetry: SEED-01 reports 5 junk artifacts to date; ROADMAP.md:197 records one regenerated mid-session on 2026-06-06

title: Structural: PostToolUse input/output contract drift across the 13 hooks — five competing field spellings (tool vs tool_name, event vs hook_event_name, tool_result vs tool_response vs tool_output, .output vs .stdout, message vs additionalContext) with no shared input normalizer; 4+ hooks silently dead or degraded as a result
causal_links: parent of D2d-03 (tool), D2d-04 (event/tool_result), D2d-05 (tool_result), D2d-08 (message), D2d-11 (.output); partial parent of D2d-02 (tool_output)
observe_how: shared/types.ts already defines the canonical PostToolUseInput (tool_name + tool_response), yet each hook re-declares its own ad-hoc input interface, and the wrong spellings type-check fine because the fields are optional. Concretely broken today: epistemic-reminder (tool), ralph-monitor (event + tool_result), ralph-task-monitor (tool_result), post-plan-roadmap (tool_output/tool_result fallback), smarter-everyday + roadmap-completion (.output-only Bash payload), agent-verification (message-only output). One shared parseHookInput()/bashOutputOf() helper in shared/ (mirroring the existing atomic-write/session-isolation helpers) plus deleting per-hook input interfaces eliminates the whole bug class and makes the 35/111-unregistered audit meaningful (a registered hook would actually run). Leverage: this is why several hooks pass their unit tests (tests feed the hook's own invented shape) while being dead in production.
telemetry: 4 hooks verified dead/degraded by this class in D2d alone; 111 hook srcs share the copy-paste input pattern
